text:
Morgan: Quick heads-up — Product is going to start a Starter->Pro migration next Tue. They expect ~35k accounts to flip over the first 72h. Rough estimate: Pro workload qps might jump ~1.6x during the ramp. Need a quick capacity/check thread. :eyes:
Priya: thanks. can you share the breakdown? is it uniform across regions or concentrated?
Morgan: mostly NA (70%), some EU (20%), APAC small. Mix of short gen (chat) and embedding-ish jobs. Models: redwood-13b and a handful of heavy 70b LLMs for enterprise tests.
Priya: OK. quick back-of-envelope: current Pro avg qps ~1.2k global. 1.6x => ~1.9k. If we keep same routing, that means more slot pressure on our p3/p4 pools. I sketched rough GPU-hours delta: 120-160 additional GPU-hours/day for 13B class and ~40-60 for 70B-class if we don't change batching.
Alex: that aligns with internal metrics. note: us-west pools already run at ~78% baseline during peak. eu-west has ~35% spare. So capacity is lumpy.
Tomas: cost sanity check: 200 extra GPU-hours/day @ avg blended $6/hr ~= $1.2k/day -> ~36k/month. We should either budget or throttle.
Lila: can we do a staged rollout? e.g., 10% canary in eu-west, 30% next day, then global? That reduces peak delta and buys time for autoscale.
Priya: staging helps. we should also consider a temporary soft-QPS cap per API key for Starter->Pro migrated users for first 72h to avoid bursty fanout. quota-bot, can you propose a soft config?
quota-bot: Proposed soft caps config (suggested):
```
soft_qps_per_key: 300 -> 450 (for migrated cohort)
burst_window_sec: 60
token_throttle: 1200/sec per key
auto-escalate: 10% every 30m if backend health ok
```
Quota-bot: Will log violations to infra-alerts and surface top offenders to #eng-oncall.
Alex: technical notes: autoscale cooldowns are 3m by default; we can tighten to 90s for p3 pools during the experiment to react faster, but that increases GPU churn. Also suggest enabling cross-region burst routing from eu-west to us-east only if latency budget allows.
Priya: adjusting cooldown to 90s + canary should keep SLOs and limit waste. I'll run a simulator this afternoon with the 1.6x profile and the soft caps. Expect numbers in ~3h.
Morgan: Product wants minimal customer friction. They asked for a low-visibility ramp but are OK with short soft caps.
Tomas: Please add estimated monthly incremental cost and a 1-week worst-case (if migration accelerates to 2x) table in the sim output. I'll flag finance for a quick budget approval.
Priya: noted. initial sim plan: baseline traffic trace window = last 30 days; multiply traffic of migrating cohort by 1.6; replay with two configs: no soft caps vs soft caps + staged rollout. Will output: peak GPU-hours/day by pool, expected 95p latency delta, estimated cost delta.
Lila: oncall checklist: create temporary runbook entries — who to page, quick-check commands, how to roll back the cohort mapping. I'll draft and push to ops-runbooks.
Alex: one more: if we see token-level hotspots, enable prefix-KV cache for chat flows for migrated users (cheap win). Will add toggle in runtime.
Priya: sim results posted: https://internal-reports/sim/1815550000 (will also paste summary here when ready) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Morgan: thanks team. action items: (1) Priya run sim + post numbers (2) Lila prepare runbook (3) Alex enable kv-cache toggle & shorter cooldowns (4) Tomas pre-approve temp budget up to $50k/mo contingency. We'll reconvene after sim. :thumbsup:
Priya: posted summary: peak extra GPU-hours (global) = 210/day, us-west extra = 140/day, eu-west extra = 45/day. With soft caps + staged rollout peak extra drops to 95/day. Estimated incremental monthly cost (no caps) = $38k/mo, with caps = $17k/mo. 95p latency impact: +6% (no caps) vs +2% (with caps).
Tomas: good detail. I'll provision a $25k/mo buffer for now and monitor. If metrics trend > +1.8x, we'll escalate to exec for additional reserve.
Morgan: consensus then: enable soft caps + staged rollout, reserve 150 GPU-hours/day in us-west for the first 72h, and run canary in eu-west. Priya and Alex to coordinate toggles. Thanks. :party-parrot:
